quote: In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that elevated INHBA enhances CRC cellular growth, migration, and invasion, whereas INHBA knockdown inhibits these malignant biological behaviors.
summary: In colorectal cancer, INHBA knockdown reduced tumour cell growth and invasion and INHBA promoted M2 macrophage polarisation; no colitis outcome was tested.

quote: A comprehensive gene expression and functional analysis was performed and identified 313 significantly altered genes, among which IL6 and INHBA were highlighted as overexpressed genes in the baseline mucosal biopsies of UCN, whose cooperation may lead to a decrease in the Tregs population.
summary: INHBA was overexpressed in baseline mucosal biopsies of UC patients who failed anti-TNF therapy and is part of a five-mRNA panel predicting non-response.

quote: Among female patients, those with any G variant in INHBA rs2237432 had a significantly longer OS than those with an A/A in both univariate (7.6 vs. 4.3 months, HR = 0.57, 95%CI = 0.34-0.95, P = 0.021) and multivariable (HR = 0.53, 95%CI = 0.29-0.94, adjusted P = 0.031) analysis.
summary: The INHBA variant rs2237432 was associated with longer survival in female metastatic colorectal cancer patients given regorafenib; not an IBD study.

quote: The induction of TGFβ1 pathway specific genes, TGFβ1, INHBA, AMHR2 and PMEPA1 was also associated with regulation of NPTX2, PDP1, SCG2, SYNPR, TAC1, TH, TNNT1 genes.
summary: INHBA is one of several TGFβ1 pathway genes induced in the striatum of dyskinetic rats; unrelated to colitis.

quote: After verification of these genes, 3 hub genes, namely CTHRC1, FNDC1, and INHBA, were found to be upregulated in tumor and associated with poor GC patient survival.
summary: INHBA was upregulated in gastric cancer and linked to poor survival, proposed as a prognostic biomarker; not a UC study.

quote: In majority of the datasets, the common DEGs found were sterile alpha motif domain containing 9 like (SAMD9L), inhibin beta A subunit (INHBA), transmembrane protein 45A (TMEM45A) and transmembrane and tetratricopeptide repeat containing 1 (TMTC1).
summary: INHBA is one of four common differentially expressed genes between IBD and ankylosing spondylitis datasets, ranked as a network hub in silico.

quote: Notably, 13 genes (CEACAM8, CEACAM6, CILP2, COL17A1, OLFM4, INHBA, LCN2, LTF, MMP8, DEFA4, PRTN3, AZU1, and ELANE) were selected for validation, and a consistent trend of increased expression in responders prior to drug administration was observed for most of these genes, with findings for 4 of them being statistically significant (CEACAM8, LCN2, LTF2, and PRTN3).
summary: INHBA was among 13 candidate blood predictors of anti-TNF response in paediatric IBD but was not among the four validated significant genes.

quote: We have also uncovered reciprocal SMAD2/3-super-enhancer-regulated feedback loops that govern expression of the TGF-β2 (TGFB2) and Activin A (INHBA) transcription units, both of which are significantly up-regulated in replicative senescence.
summary: INHBA (activin A) is up-regulated in replicative senescence and drives proliferation arrest; not related to colitis.

quote: The findings underscore the potential of INHBA, MMP7, PSAT1, SLC7A5, and TGFBI as effective non-invasive biomarkers for CRC detection.
summary: Serum INHBA was higher in colorectal cancer patients than in healthy controls and showed diagnostic accuracy as part of a five-marker set.

quote: Key transcription factors associated with reproductive function included INHBA (ovary), KITLG (oviduct), Snai2 (cervix), WNT7A (uterine horn), FOLR1 (uterine body), and SALL1 (shared uterine regions).
summary: INHBA is listed among key reproductive transcription factors in a sheep enhancer atlas; unrelated to UC.

quote: Notably, INHBA knockdown suppressed ECSS cell migration and invasion and altered the expression of important apoptotic and survival proteins.
summary: INHBA knockdown reduced migration and invasion of oesophageal squamous carcinoma cells; no inflammation or colitis outcome.

quote: Expression of p-EMT markers (SPP1, EMP3, INHBA, THBS2, ITGA5, P4HA2) and EMT-markers (ZEB1, SNAI1) was analyzed via RT-PCR after 6 hours (h) and 24 h.
summary: INHBA is one of several partial-EMT markers measured in colorectal cancer cells infected with oral bacteria, with no specific INHBA result highlighted.

quote: Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis revealed 10 hub genes (LIFR, CNTFR, LIF, CSF2, IL1A, CSF3, F2, FGA, FGFR2, INHBA).
summary: INHBA is one of ten glycoprotein-related hub genes in colon adenocarcinoma; the paper focuses on FJX1.

quote: The expression level of the oncogenes associated with mortality, SNAI1, THBS2 and INHBA reduced to 0.74, 0.66 and 0.7 folds, respectively.
summary: Nanoparticle treatment lowered INHBA expression in SW480 colorectal cancer cells; no UC relevance.

quote: In colon and stomach cancers, increased INHBA expression significantly correlates with poorer overall survival (OS).
summary: INHBA is upregulated across most gastrointestinal cancers in TCGA data and higher expression correlates with worse survival in colon and stomach cancer.

quote: These genes showed strong discriminatory performance (AUC > 0.85), and Random Forest analysis further refined a seven-gene panel (FAP, TIMP1, COL12A1, CALU, INHBA, SPP1, and CTHRC1).
summary: INHBA is one of seven genes in an EMT signature distinguishing UC-associated neoplasia from quiescent UC; no INHBA-specific result.

quote: Supplementation with activin A restored IL-17A and  Rorc expression during pathogenic Th17 cell differentiation.
summary: Inhba (activin A) is a JunB target and recombinant activin A restored IL-17A and Rorc during pathogenic Th17 differentiation, suggesting it supports Th17 pathogenicity.

quote: However, over the past decade, marked advances in the treatment of metastatic RCC have been made, with targeted agents including sorafenib, sunitinib, bevacizumab, pazopanib and axitinib, which inhibit vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and its receptor (VEGFR), and everolimus and temsirolimus, which inhibit mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), being approved.
summary: Renal cell carcinoma review noting VEGFR-inhibiting drugs are approved for metastatic disease; nothing on UC or colitis.
The paper concerns VEGFR-3 and lymphatic growth in airway inflammation, not KDR/VEGFR2.

quote: The most common drug targets of the approved pharmaceuticals include BCR-Abl, B-Raf, vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFR), epidermal growth factor receptors (EGFR), and ALK.
summary: Review of FDA-approved kinase inhibitors that lists VEGFR among the most common targets; no UC-specific data on KDR.

quote: Lenvatinib is a multikinase inhibitor of VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3, and other receptor tyrosine kinases.
summary: Phase 2 endometrial cancer trial of the multikinase inhibitor lenvatinib with pembrolizumab; VEGFR2 is only one of several targets and no colitis outcome is tested.

quote: The most common drug targets include ALK, B-Raf, BCR-Abl, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR).
summary: Review of FDA-approved kinase inhibitors that lists VEGFR among the common targets; no UC-specific data on KDR.

quote: Foretinib is an oral multikinase inhibitor targeting MET, VEGF, RON, AXL, and TIE-2 receptors.
summary: Phase II trial of the MET/VEGFR2 inhibitor foretinib in papillary renal carcinoma; efficacy tracked with MET mutation, with nothing on VEGFR2 or colitis.

quote: Interleukin 4Rα, VEGFR, CD15 and CD66b have been suggested to be more specific markers for human MDSC, however these markers can only be found on some MDSC subsets.
summary: Review of myeloid-derived suppressor cells in human disease noting VEGFR as a proposed marker; no UC data.

quote: Flow cytometry analyses of these cultured cells at passage 4 showed expression of typical MSC markers such as CD44 and CD29, but not hematopoietic markers such as c-kit, flk1, and CD34.
summary: Cultured mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells did not express flk1, used only as a negative cell-identity marker; unrelated to colitis.
